correctness.rationale: For 0<p<1/2, exact conditional attachment probabilities are P(Delta L=+1)=[p+(1-p)(L+S)]/n and P(Delta L=-1)=[pL+(1-p)L/D]/n, with S=sum_{nonleaf neighbours u}1/D(u)>=0 and L<=D. Hence conditional drift is [(1-2p)(L-1)+(1-p)(1-L/D+S)]/n. For Y=(L-1)_+, when L>=2 the increment equals Delta L; for L<=1, Y next is nonnegative. Therefore E[Y_(n+1)|F_n]>=(1+(1-2p)/n)Y_n. Seed events occur with probabilities p/2 at n=3 for v=1,2 and p^2/[v(v+1)] at n=v+2 for v>=3, giving positive expected Y. Gamma-product iteration implies liminf n^-(1-2p) E Y >= b Gamma(m)/Gamma(m+1-2p) >0. Independently enumerated 11,824 exact rational conditional-transition/difference checks on growing finite trees; no finite experiment is used as an infinite-time proof.

value.rationale: The mixed random-friend-tree model is a natural interpolation between uniform recursive attachment and one-step redirection. An explicit polynomial lower bound on leaf-neighbour excess for each fixed vertex answers a local quantitative question not settled by qualitative degree divergence or global leaf density. Although proof uses an elementary drift inequality, it is a motivated infinite-horizon growth theorem with explicit constants, not just an algebraic sign check.
